clue.text: See 21
Intricate pieces from flugelhorn at Eisteddfod

indicators.note: pieces taken from the run of words flugelhorn at Eisteddfod, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A brass player performs something elaborate at the Welsh festival of music and poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry, which suits the flugelhorn; the answer runs across the end of flugelhorn, all of at and the start of Eisteddfod.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is elaborately decorated, so intricate is a close synonym.

clue.text: Revered idea broadcast around area of country from the beginning

indicators.note: around means the word for broadcast goes on both sides of the other pieces

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it, scattering it widely
an acre is a measured area of land
DC stands for da capo, the musical direction meaning play again from the beginning

explanation.surface: An idea everyone reveres has been spread across a whole region of the land since the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the beginning' looks like a direction to take first letters, but it is D.C., da capo, the musical instruction to go back to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is a belief or institution held to be beyond criticism, an idea treated as untouchable.

clue.text: Ignorant of Stubbs pottery?

parts.note: Una Stubbs was an English actress, known for Till Death Us Do Part and Sherlock
ware means pottery, as in earthenware or Wedgwood ware

explanation.surface: Someone who has never heard of Stubbs's ceramics, with a question mark for the invented pottery brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Stubbs suggests the painter George Stubbs, or Stubbs pottery, but it is Una Stubbs, a British TV actress; the question mark marks the joke of a pottery line named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unaware of something is to be ignorant of it, having no knowledge of it.

clue.text: Rotate chunk of rafter I failed to get burning

indicators.note: rotate tells you to turn the hidden letters round so they read the other way
a chunk of the words rafter I failed means letters lifted from inside them

explanation.surface: A carpenter told to turn a section of beam, having failed, sets it alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chunk of' takes ERIFA from the end of rafter, I and the start of failed; 'Rotate' turns those letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire is an old-fashioned adjective for being on fire, or ablaze.

clue.text: Fruit with no varieties?

parts.note: no means nothing, shown by the letter O, a zero
a range is a variety or assortment, as in a range of products

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a fruit that comes in only one kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the definition to the wordplay; 'no varieties' reads as O (zero) followed by a word for varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are a citrus fruit, so the plural fruit word fits as an example.

clue.text: Perhaps maiden aircraftwoman Hughes performed unsatisfactorily

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over from which no runs are scored, so it is perhaps an over
AC is the RAF rank abbreviation for aircraftman, used here for aircraftwoman
Ted Hughes was a British Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A young woman in the air force named Hughes gave a poor performance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like an unmarried young woman, but in cricket a maiden is a scoreless over. Ted Hughes is the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to exaggerate a role, a kind of poor performance on stage.

clue.text: Modifies starters of any dodgy automobiles prone to stalling

indicators.note: starters of means the first letter of each of the next six words

explanation.surface: Someone changes the first parts of any unreliable cars that keep stalling.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to alter it to suit a new purpose, so it modifies.

clue.text: Snapper's Centre Of Photography atop a hill

indicators.note: the centre of the word Photography is its sixth letter, in the middle of eleven

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A capitalised name for a photography centre on top of a hill, with Snapper as a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: Snapper looks like a photographer, matching the photography centre, but it is an animal with snapping jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A gator, short for alligator, is a reptile with powerful jaws that snap shut.

clue.text: Formally withdrawing club's initial rating of player as a guard

indicators.note: as a guard means the word for rating of player stands around the club letter, guarding it

parts.note: seeding ranks a player in a tournament draw

indicators.note: the initial of club is its first letter

explanation.surface: A club's first ranking of a player as a defender in some team sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a guard' looks like a playing position, but it means one piece guards, that is surrounds, the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union or federation, as states did in the US Civil War.

clue.text: Peach tree canine almost trashed

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order
almost means the word canine loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A dog has nearly wrecked a peach tree in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims canine to CANIN; 'trashed' rearranges those letters together with TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of the peach tree's fruit.

clue.text: Old American found in middle of piazza by investigator

indicators.note: the middle of piazza is its central pair of letters, the third and fourth of six

parts.note: tec is short for detective, an investigator

explanation.surface: An ancient American turned up in the middle of an Italian square by a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the pre-Columbian people who ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Support elderly horse at end of life, not yet 20

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball
a nag is an old or worn-out horse

indicators.note: the end of life is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone props up an old horse as it nears death, though its keeper is still a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes the years from thirteen to nineteen, an age short of twenty.

clue.text: Changed key before commencement of diminuendo

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the commencement of diminuendo is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musical score shifts key just before the music starts to grow quieter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a musical key, matching diminuendo, but it is the Alt key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, so altered is a direct synonym of changed.

clue.text: Brown oil damaged E-scooter

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of E-scooter are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dark oil has been spilled from an electric scooter that is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a dark brown oily liquid from tar, painted on fences as wood preservative.

clue.text: Very unusual hut provides roof for European in remote location

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the European, acting as its roof

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of hut are set in an odd order

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European

explanation.surface: A very odd hut gives shelter to a European out in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges hut to UTH; in a down answer, being a roof for something means coming above it.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Pole lies at the bottom of the Earth in Antarctica, among the most isolated places there are.

clue.text: Story of beam reflected by Newton

indicators.note: reflected means sent back, so the word for beam is read backwards

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: An account of how Isaac Newton bent a beam of light back with a mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton suggests Isaac Newton and his optics, but here it is N, the symbol for the unit of force named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long, often far-fetched tale, so it is an informal word for a story.

clue.text: Current inside Neptunian satellite, after a time, is wearing down

indicators.note: after means the moon part comes after a and the time letter
inside means the current letter goes within the name of the moon

parts.note: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electric current is flowing within one of Neptune's moons, and over time it is eroding.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrition is the gradual weakening or erosion of something by friction or constant pressure.

clue.text: Mixing with that guy's family before midnight

indicators.note: before means the family word comes ahead of the midnight letter

parts.note: his means belonging to that guy
kin means family or relatives
midnight read as mid night, the middle letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A man stirs something with his relatives late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: Midnight is split as mid night: the middle letter of night, a G.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisking means beating ingredients together quickly, a way of mixing them in cooking.

clue.text: Shout about selling bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... goods is to sell them by calling out in the street
second meaning: a bird of prey

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a reversal or containment signal, but it belongs to the definition: to shout about what you are selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Street vendors hawk wares by crying them aloud, and the same word names a bird of prey.

clue.text: Sixties designer adopting a doctor's measuring device

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the designer's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Mary Quant was the 1960s British fashion designer behind the miniskirt
DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A fashion designer of the 1960s takes up a device belonging to a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is an old instrument for measuring angles and altitudes, used in navigation and astronomy.

clue.text: Fault in a drilling platform cropping up

indicators.note: in means the fault word goes inside the platform word

parts.note: a rig is an oil-drilling platform
a sin is a fault or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A fault turns up on an oil rig.
explanation.definitionFit: Arising means coming into being or emerging, so it means appearing unexpectedly.

clue.text: Fan cures Obama in dilapidated car showroom?

indicators.note: in means the reworked cures Obama goes inside the reworked car
dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters of car are rearranged
to fan things is to spread them out, so the letters of cures Obama are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A supporter fixes up Obama's broken-down car in a dealer's showroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' reads as a supporter, but it is the signal to spread out cures Obama; that sits inside CRA, from 'dilapidated' car.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera obscura is a darkened chamber projecting an image of the outside scene, literally a room that shows things.

clue.text: Ultimate tragic gamester heartily makes digital duplicate

indicators.note: heartily means the heart of each word, the central pair of letters of Ultimate, tragic and gamester

explanation.surface: The ultimate gambler with a tragic end makes a copy of something on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartily' looks like an adverb meaning enthusiastically, but it applies to all three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To image a disk is to make an exact digital copy of its contents.

clue.text: Tolerate second coat amid very warm easterly

indicators.note: amid means the coat word sits in the middle of the other word
in an across clue, travelling easterly means right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: hot means very warm
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: Putting up with a second coat during a hot spell from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easterly' reverses HOT to TOH, and the mac goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it, an idiom from being able to digest it.

clue.text: Transmitting booming Tallis aria frequently

indicators.note: frequently means at regular intervals, here every third letter of booming Tallis aria

explanation.surface: A loud aria by the Tudor composer Thomas Tallis is often broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every third letter of booming Tallis aria, starting with its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is being broadcast, so it means transmitting.

clue.text: Is "jam in roly-poly" a form of worship?

indicators.note: roly-poly suggests rolling over and over, so the letters of Is jam in are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether jam rolled inside a pudding counts as a religion.
explanation.walkthrough: A roly-poly is a British suet pudding rolled with jam, but here it is the signal to roll the letters about.
explanation.definitionFit: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion stressing non-violence toward all living things.

clue.text: Extract battery power

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the liquid extracted from fruit
second meaning: informal for electric power, as from a battery

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names liquid squeezed out of fruit and, informally, electricity or fuel.

clue.text: Silly chicken animator's segment runs backwards

indicators.note: runs backwards means the lifted letters are read in reverse order
a segment of chicken animator is a run of letters lifted from inside the words

explanation.surface: A cartoonist's foolish chicken sequence plays in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'segment' takes ENANI from the end of chicken and the start of animator; 'runs backwards' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or empty-headed, a close synonym of silly.

clue.text: Rusting unopened container concealed gluey material for stiffening fabric

indicators.note: unopened means each of the three words that follow loses its first letter

parts.note: a box is a container
hid means concealed
size is a gluey wash used to stiffen fabric or paper, and sizing is the same material

explanation.surface: A sealed container hid some starchy paste for stiffening cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' beheads all three words: BOX, HID and SIZING lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust forms when iron oxidizes, so rusting is a kind of oxidizing.

clue.text: Bachelor inhabiting lock-up can type

indicators.note: inhabiting means living inside, so the bachelor letter goes within the lock-up

parts.note: a lock-up is a garage rented for storing a car
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: A single man lives in a rented garage and can type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can type' looks like a typist's skill, but can is a noun: a garbage can is a type of can. A lock-up is British for a rented garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbage can is a kind of bin, so garbage describes one variety of can.

clue.text: Bonnet-wearing drivers?

parts.note: a car bonnet is the hinged hood over the motor, so the things under it that drive the car wear the bonnet

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of motorists in Easter bonnets; the drivers are what powers the car. The bonnet is the British name for a car's hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Car motors sit under the hood and provide the driving force, so they are the machines that drive.
